taxonomy_source.version: PFCv2 (superset of PFCv1); every PFCv1 detailed category from https://plaid.com/documents/transactions-personal-finance-category-taxonomy.csv is also mapped
taxonomy_source.default_version_note: Plaid teams enabled for Transactions on or after 3 Dec 2025 get PFCv2 only (Sandbox and Production alike); older teams get v1 unless they send options.personal_finance_category_version='v2'. Each transaction's personal_finance_category.version says which it is.

note_on_how_issuers_decide: Rewards categories are decided by merchant category codes (MCCs), not by what you bought. When a merchant signs up to accept cards, it (or its acquirer/processor) is assigned a 4-digit MCC under the card networks' rules, based on what the business primarily sells. Every purchase reaches the issuer carrying that merchant's MCC, and the issuer groups MCCs into its bonus categories. Chase: merchants are 'assigned a merchant code, which is determined by the merchant or its processor in accordance with Visa/Mastercard procedures based on the kinds of products and services they primarily sell. We group similar merchant codes into categories'; if 'the merchant may not have a merchant code in that category', 'purchases with that merchant won't qualify'. Citi: 'We don't control the assignment of these codes... When you use your card to make a purchase, we're provided an MCC for that purchase.' Amex: 'Merchants are assigned codes based on what they primarily sell. A purchase will not qualify for additional points if the merchant's code is not eligible'. Consequences: buying groceries at Target or Walmart (5310/5311 superstores) or Costco (5300 warehouse club) does not earn a supermarket bonus (Amex: 'Superstores, convenience stores, warehouse clubs, and meal-kit delivery services are NOT considered supermarkets'; Chase and Citi say the same); fuel bought at a warehouse club or superstore is not 'gas' at Amex ('Superstores, supermarkets, and warehouse clubs that sell gasoline are NOT considered gas stations') or at Citi unless coded with the gas-station MCC; a restaurant inside a hotel, stadium or store can carry the host's code; a purchase through PayPal or another aggregator can carry the aggregator's code. Some categories are named merchant lists rather than MCC sets (Chase and Amex streaming, Amex drugstores), and 'online retail' has no MCC at all (issuers rely on the merchant's internet-transaction flag). Plaid's personal_finance_category is Plaid's own model output, inferred from the transaction description, merchant and amount, with a confidence_level; Plaid's Transactions API does not return the MCC. So a PFC can disagree with the MCC the issuer sees (e.g. Plaid calls a Walmart grocery run FOOD_AND_DRINK_GROCERIES or GENERAL_MERCHANDISE_SUPERSTORES, while the issuer sees 5310). Treat any category this map produces as an estimate of what the issuer will pay, and prefer the issuer's statement category when available.
how_to_apply: 1. Skip transactions with a negative amount on a credit account (Plaid: positive = money out, negative = refunds/payments).
2. Run merchant_overrides (first match wins) against merchant_name, then against name/original_description, after stripping descriptor_prefixes.
3. Else use detailed_map[personal_finance_category.detailed]; else primary_map[primary]; else everything_else.
4. exclude: true means not reward-eligible spend (income, transfers, payments, fees).
5. Entries with merchant_dependent or review flags are low-confidence; show them to the user.

INCOME.note: Money coming in, not a card purchase; earns no rewards.

TRANSFER_IN.note: Movement of money between accounts, not a purchase; earns no rewards.

TRANSFER_OUT.note: Movement of money between accounts, not a purchase; earns no rewards.

LOAN_PAYMENTS.note: Debt repayment (including paying the credit card itself); not a purchase, earns no rewards.

LOAN_DISBURSEMENTS.note: Loan or advance deposited to the user; not a purchase.

BANK_FEES.note: Bank or card fee/interest; issuers exclude fees and interest from rewards.

ENTERTAINMENT.note: Fallback only; TV/movies and music detailed categories go to streaming.

FOOD_AND_DRINK.note: Fallback only; groceries and liquor stores differ at the detailed level.

GENERAL_MERCHANDISE.note: Fallback only; online marketplaces -> online_retail, superstores -> merchant name.

HOME_IMPROVEMENT.note: Fallback only; furniture and services are everything_else at the detailed level.

MEDICAL.note: Fallback only; pharmacies -> drugstores at the detailed level.

TRANSPORTATION.note: Fallback only; always use the detailed category (gas, transit, rideshare split there).

TRAVEL.note: Fallback only; flights -> airfare, lodging -> hotels at the detailed level.

RENT_AND_UTILITIES.note: Fallback only; rent and telephone split at the detailed level.

ENTERTAINMENT_CASINOS_AND_GAMBLING.note: Betting codes MCC 7995, which issuers generally exclude from entertainment and often treat as a cash advance. Consider exclude for reward estimates.

ENTERTAINMENT_MUSIC_AND_AUDIO.note: Plaid includes in-person music purchases here too. Use merchant_overrides: subscription services (Spotify, Apple Music, Pandora, SiriusXM...) are streaming; concert tickets (Ticketmaster, Live Nation) are entertainment. Issuers' streaming categories are usually a named merchant list (Chase, Amex).

ENTERTAINMENT_OTHER_ENTERTAINMENT.note: Includes nightlife; bars usually code MCC 5813 and earn as dining at many issuers, so a dining override by merchant name may fit better.

ENTERTAINMENT_TV_AND_MOVIES.note: Plaid puts in-home streaming AND movie theaters here. Default to streaming; merchant name decides: theaters (AMC, Regal, Cinemark, Fandango) are entertainment (MCC 7832).

ENTERTAINMENT_VIDEO_GAMES.note: Digital game purchases code MCC 5816 (Digital Goods - Games), which issuer entertainment and streaming categories generally do not include.

FOOD_AND_DRINK_BEER_WINE_AND_LIQUOR.note: Liquor stores code MCC 5921; issuers exclude them from supermarkets (Amex) and dining.

FOOD_AND_DRINK_COFFEE.note: Coffee shops code as restaurants/fast food (5812/5814) at most issuers; a cafe inside a grocery store or retailer takes that store's code.

FOOD_AND_DRINK_GROCERIES.note: Superstores (Target, Walmart) and warehouse clubs are a separate PFC (GENERAL_MERCHANDISE_SUPERSTORES); online grocery delivery has no PFC, see merchant_overrides.

FOOD_AND_DRINK_OTHER_FOOD_AND_DRINK.note: Desserts, juice bars, delis. Bakeries (5462) and candy stores (5441) are excluded from both dining and supermarkets by Citi and Amex, so this is optimistic.

GENERAL_MERCHANDISE_CONVENIENCE_STORES.note: If the store also sells fuel and codes 5541/5542 it earns as gas (Amex: 'You may earn additional rewards if the gas station is also a convenience store').

GENERAL_MERCHANDISE_ELECTRONICS.note: Online electronics stores may count as online_retail at issuers with an online-retail category; Plaid does not say whether the purchase was online (check payment_channel == 'online').

GENERAL_MERCHANDISE_ONLINE_MARKETPLACES.note: Amazon, eBay, Etsy. There is no MCC for 'online retail': Amex, Capital One and others decide from the merchant's own online/card-not-present flag and their own lists.

GENERAL_MERCHANDISE_SUPERSTORES.note: Plaid lumps superstores (Target, Walmart; MCC 5310/5311) with warehouse clubs (Costco, Sam's Club, BJ's; MCC 5300). Merchant name decides: a club match in merchant_overrides gives wholesale_clubs, otherwise everything_else. Issuers exclude both from groceries (Amex, Chase, Citi).

GOVERNMENT_AND_NON_PROFIT_TAX_PAYMENT.note: Tax payments (MCC 9311) usually go through a processor that charges about 2%; the fee usually outweighs base rewards.

HOME_IMPROVEMENT_FURNITURE.note: Furniture stores code MCC 5712, which home-improvement categories (5200/5211/5231/5251/5261) usually exclude.

HOME_IMPROVEMENT_HARDWARE.note: Home Depot/Lowe's code 5200; hardware stores 5251; lumber 5211.

HOME_IMPROVEMENT_OTHER_HOME_IMPROVEMENT.note: Pool installation, pest control: services, not store MCCs.

HOME_IMPROVEMENT_REPAIR_AND_MAINTENANCE.note: Low confidence: garden centers (5261) qualify, but plumbers, roofers and other contractors code as contractor MCCs (e.g. 1711, 1761) that issuer home-improvement categories generally exclude.

HOME_IMPROVEMENT_SECURITY.note: Alarm/security services are not home-improvement-store MCCs.

RENT_AND_UTILITIES_INTERNET_AND_CABLE.note: Cable TV shares MCC 4899 with streaming services; internet providers often code 4814/4816. Issuers that bonus 'streaming' by MCC can therefore pay out on cable.

RENT_AND_UTILITIES_RENT.note: Most landlords don't take cards, or charge a fee via a processor; rent rewards realistically come from Bilt's own payment rails. Paying rent from a bank account (ACH) is not card spend at all.

TRANSPORTATION_GAS.note: Plaid may also put EV charging here; Tesla Supercharger/ChargePoint/Electrify America/EVgo are ev_charging via merchant_overrides (MCC 5552). Fuel at warehouse clubs and superstores is excluded from gas by Amex and Citi.

TRANSPORTATION_PARKING.note: Parking (MCC 7523) is inside Chase's travel/transit definition and some others; issuers differ.

TRANSPORTATION_PUBLIC_TRANSIT.note: MCC 4111 commuter transport/ferries, 4112 passenger rail, 4131 bus lines.

TRANSPORTATION_TAXIS_AND_RIDE_SHARES.note: Uber/Lyft/taxis code MCC 4121. Uber Eats is food delivery, not rideshare: merchant_overrides puts it in dining.

TRANSPORTATION_TOLLS.note: Tolls (MCC 4784) count as transit/travel at Chase and some others; issuers differ.

TRAVEL_FLIGHTS.note: Airlines code 3000-3350 or 4511. If booked through an issuer portal it earns travel_portal; Plaid can't tell (booking channel).

TRAVEL_LODGING.note: Hotels code 3501-3999 or 7011. Airbnb/VRBO coding varies by processor. Portal bookings: see travel_portal note.

TRAVEL_OTHER_TRAVEL.note: Travel agencies/tour operators (4722) and cruise lines; counts as 'travel' on general travel cards, not airfare or hotels.

TRAVEL_RENTAL_CARS.note: No rental-car slot in the app vocabulary; rental agencies code 3351-3500 or 7512 and earn as 'travel' on general travel cards.

dining.note: Citi excludes caterers and bakeries from restaurants; Amex excludes bars, nightclubs, caterers and restaurants inside other venues. 5813 is dining at some issuers only.

online_groceries.note: No dedicated MCC. Online grocery earns only if the delivery merchant codes as a grocery store (Chase: 'delivery service merchants that classify as grocery store merchants'; Citi: online supermarkets 'do not qualify if the merchant does not classify itself as a supermarket'). Decide by merchant name.

travel_portal.note: No MCC or PFC identifies an issuer travel portal; the bonus depends on the booking channel (Chase Travel, Amex Travel, Capital One Travel, Citi Travel). The app must ask the user or match portal descriptors it has verified.

superstores.note: Not an app category (they map to everything_else). Target and Walmart typically code here, which is why they don't earn grocery bonuses even though they sell groceries.

online_retail.note: No MCC means 'online'. Issuers use their own rules: Amex says 'To identify eligible online retail purchases, we rely on information provided to us by the merchant' and requires payment to be 'categorized as an internet transaction by the merchant'. Capital One and Citi use their own merchant lists and card-not-present flags. Plaid's payment_channel ('online', 'in store', 'other') is the nearest signal.
